title: performance (T3). Each in-between picture is a full CPU walk and a full GPU frame.
note: Design (read 11-18, E6b with I-002 and P-156): an in-between picture differs from its list's step picture only in the blended rows (transforms, the camera's view) and in which items a moved bound culls. So each draw pass is recorded once per list, at its first picture (DrawRecorder ops, draw_record.h), with every row read through the rows base (encoder set_rows, walk_.rows_address) as the one patched value; an in-between picture writes its blended rows into a new rows slice and replays the recorded ops with that base: no walk of the items, no material or pipeline lookups. Culling: an item culled at both ends of the pair stays culled (the bound's union over the pair, a test at record time), so a replay never misses one; items culled at one end only are recorded and drawn. Passes whose inputs do not depend on t (2D layers not marked present-time, the frame copy of a step picture) are replayed as recorded. The GPU work stays a full frame (a new picture of moved objects); its cost is P-156's, measured per pass. Proof: the timeline's Walk events (b=1 in-between) on the PC at 240 Hz and the tablet at 120 Hz: render-thread time of an in-between picture before and after; the interpolation tours' pictures the same. 11-19 (FRAME-MODEL 2.16, E6b read at 241395b49 and rows/i016 697535a86): placed in E6b's landing 8; 2.16's rows table says what it does for this row.
